issues.description: Return type mismatch for PersonService.addParent: the problem statement and the template expect addParent(Person, Person) to return the persisted Person (and the template's PersonResource and tests assign the method result to a variable), but the solution implementation declares addParent(...) as void. This creates a structural contradiction in the solution: PersonResource and the unit tests call/assign the return value of addParent, and the solution's void method therefore cannot be used as written (would not compile / will break tests).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution's PersonService.addParent method match the template/problem expectation by returning a Person. For example, change its signature to 'public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent)' and return the persisted person (e.g. 'return personRepository.save(person);'). This aligns the service implementation with PersonResource and the tests and resolves the compile/test failures.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect PersonService.addParent(Person person, Person parent) to return the saved Person (the problem text explicitly says the method should return the result of save(..) and the template declares a Person return type). In the solution repository, PersonService.addParent is implemented with a void return type. Meanwhile PersonResource (and the tests) call person = personService.addParent(...) and therefore expect a Person to be returned. This mismatch between the expected return type (Person) and the solution implementation (void) creates a semantic/API inconsistency that will confuse students mapping the requirement to the implementation and will break compilation/usage of the service from the resource/tests.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the service API with the problem statement and template. Change the solution implementation of addParent to return Person (signature: public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent)) and at the end return personRepository.save(person); This ensures PersonResource and tests can assign the returned Person and matches the documented/expected behavior.
